passage: The assembly hall was packed for the science fair, and the noise was so loud that Ritu, the class teacher, had to lean in to hear anyone. She saw Kalyani near the door in a neat uniform, smiling slightly at everyone who passed. But the smile stayed at her mouth. Her eyes were flat, and she kept checking her phone. Ritu had seen Kalyani laugh loudly in Class 9. Now she did not join her friends. Between two announcements, Ritu said, "I have to run this, but I am free after lunch if you ever want tea." Kalyani said, "I am fine, Miss," with the same smile. Ritu nodded. "The door is open."

qa.q: What was happening in the assembly hall?
qa.a: The assembly hall was packed for the science fair.

qa.q: What made Ritu wonder about Kalyani's smile?
qa.a: The smile stayed at her mouth while her eyes were flat, and she did not join her friends, which fits poorly with the laugh Ritu had seen before. It might just be tiredness, so Ritu did not assume.

qa.q: How did Ritu offer help without pressure?
qa.a: She said she was free after lunch and that the door was open, and accepted "I am fine" without pushing.

qa.q: How might Kalyani have felt hearing Ritu's offer?
qa.a: She might feel a little seen and relieved someone noticed, or she might feel exposed, which is why the low-pressure offer matters. 🤍

grounding: A teenager keeps a slight smile while feeling low to avoid questions, and a trusted adult offers an open door without pressure.

passage: At dinner, Mahima passed the dal and smiled, right on time, as always. Her mother Sharmila noticed the smile was smaller than usual and did not reach her eyes. She had also left half her chapati. When Sharmila asked about the school trip, Mahima said, "Fine, it was fun," and looked at her plate. Sharmila did not push. She said, "I am doing the dishes late tonight, and you can come and dry if you want. Or not." Later that evening, the tap ran, the dishes clinked, and Mahima appeared quietly in the kitchen. She picked up a towel and stood there for a long while without speaking.

qa.q: What did Mahima leave half-eaten at dinner?
qa.a: Mahima left half of her chapati.

qa.q: What might Sharmila have been worried about when she saw Mahima's smaller smile?
qa.a: She may have worried that Mahima was low, since the smile was smaller than usual, did not reach her eyes and came with a half-eaten chapati. It might have been tiredness, so she left room to check.

qa.q: How did Sharmila leave the door open without pressure?
qa.a: She invited Mahima to help dry the dishes if she wanted, and said "or not", so there was no demand.

qa.q: How might Mahima feel when she picks up the towel and stands quietly?
qa.a: She probably wants company and is deciding whether to speak, so being with her mother without pressure is helpful.

grounding: A teenager masks sadness with a smile, and a parent offers a gentle open door.

passage:
"Farida, stay back a minute."
"Yes, Ma'am?"
"You smiled all through the lesson."
"Is that bad?" A small laugh.
"No. But your eyes didn't smile, and you haven't eaten lunch with Sana and Mehr all week."
Farida looked down at her notebook. "I'm fine. Really."
"Okay." Lalremsiami Ma'am didn't push. "I'm not going to make you talk. But I'm in this room every lunch break. You can come and just sit, if you like. No questions."
"Even if I don't want to talk?"
"Even then. And if you ever want someone else, the counsellor is next door."
Farida nodded. The smile stayed, but it wobbled a little.
The next day at lunch, she came and sat by the window with her tiffin. Ma'am just said, "Hi," and went on marking.

qa.q: Where did Farida sit the next day at lunch?
qa.a: By the window with her tiffin.

qa.q: What does Farida's wobbling smile suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: It suggests she was feeling low and sad but trying to hide it, and the teacher's kindness nearly broke through.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami Ma'am do that was helpful?
qa.a: She noticed the smile didn't reach Farida's eyes, gently mentioned it, and offered an open door without pressure.

qa.q: How might Sana and Mehr see Farida's change?
qa.a: They might feel puzzled or worried that Farida stopped eating with them, not knowing she was feeling low.

grounding: A teacher notices a teenager's smile doesn't match other cues and offers a gentle open door without pressure.

passage:
The year my parents separated, I kept smiling at school. Every day, same smile. I thought if I looked fine, no one would ask questions, and I wouldn't have to explain.
But Anjali Ma'am, my maths teacher, noticed. One day she said quietly after class, "Thomas, you've been smiling a lot, but your eyes look tired. If you ever want to talk, I'm here after school on Thursdays."
I said, "Thanks, I'm okay." But I thought about it all week.
The next Thursday, I went. I didn't say much. She just let me sit and do homework in her room. After three Thursdays, I told her about my parents.
She didn't fix it. She just listened, and asked if I wanted to see the counsellor too. I did.
- Thomas

qa.q: Which day was Anjali Ma'am available after school?
qa.a: Thursdays.

qa.q: What was Thomas feeling behind the smile at school?
qa.a: Thomas felt sad and low about the parents' separation, but hid it to avoid questions.

qa.q: What did Anjali Ma'am do that fits a gentle open door?
qa.a: She noticed the tired eyes, offered a regular time to come without pressure, listened when Thomas was ready, and offered the counsellor.

qa.q: How might Anjali Ma'am have felt when Thomas finally talked?
qa.a: She probably felt relieved and glad that Thomas trusted her enough to share.

grounding: The narrator recalls masking sadness with a smile, and a teacher noticing and offering a gentle open door.

passage:
Counsellor's note, Wednesday
Anirban's class teacher, Vijay Sir, mentioned that Anirban has been smiling in class but eats alone, looks tired, and his grades have slipped this term.
I invited Anirban for a chat. He smiled the whole time and said everything was fine. But the smile didn't reach his eyes, and he kept pulling at his sleeves.
I didn't press. I told him I'm available every Tuesday and Friday, and he can come for any reason, even just to sit.
With Anirban's knowledge, I will call his parents this evening to share that we're keeping an eye out, and Vijay Sir will check in with him daily.
- Ms Pinto, school counsellor

qa.q: What days is Ms Pinto available?
qa.a: Every Tuesday and Friday.

qa.q: What might Anirban have been feeling behind his smile?
qa.a: He was probably sad and low but hiding it, since his smile didn't reach his eyes and he pulled at his sleeves.

qa.q: What steps did Ms Pinto take to help?
qa.a: She offered a regular open door without pressure, planned to call his parents that evening with his knowledge, and asked Vijay Sir to check in daily.

qa.q: How might Vijay Sir see Anirban's smile after talking to the counsellor?
qa.a: He would likely watch more closely, seeing it as a possible mask rather than a sign that all is well.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows adults noticing a teenager's smile hiding low mood and offering support without pressure.

passage:
Thursday, late
Smiled all day again. Smiled at the bus stop, smiled in chemistry, smiled when Ritika showed me her new bag. It's easier than people asking what's wrong, because I don't even know what's wrong, only that everything has felt grey since Nani passed in March.
Then in the library, Pradeep Sir handed back my essay and said, "Good work. You look tired these days, though. The smile's there, but the rest of you isn't." I laughed it off. He didn't push. He just said, "My room's open at lunch on Tuesdays and Fridays, if you ever want somewhere quiet. Talk or don't talk."
I nearly cried in the corridor. When I got home I told Mumma about the grey feeling. She held my hand for a long time and said we'd go and see the school counsellor together.
Himani

qa.q: When did Nani pass away?
qa.a: In March.

qa.q: Why did Himani keep smiling all day?
qa.a: Himani felt low and grey but kept smiling to avoid questions, partly because the sadness was hard to explain even to Himani.

qa.q: What made Pradeep Sir's approach work?
qa.a: He named what he saw kindly, didn't press, and offered a clear, low-pressure time to come, whether to talk or just sit.

qa.q: What might Pradeep Sir have noticed?
qa.a: He noticed the smile didn't match the tiredness in the rest of Himani's face, and chose a gentle offer instead of questions.

grounding: It shows a teenager masking low mood with a smile and a trusted adult noticing that it doesn't reach the rest of the face, offering an open door without pressure.
